title: Exactness data for the ringed-topos projection mate
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small ringed sites, with sheaves of commutative rings and a ring map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Use the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Derived tensor is computed by replacing one factor by a K-flat resolution. Write $L=Lf^*$ for derived extension of scalars after inverse image and $R=Rf_*$ for the derived direct image computed using K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], with their canonical derived adjunction and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to1$. Derived tensor is exact in each variable. The canonical pullback tensor isomorphism
$$\mu_{M,N}:L(M\otimes^L_{R_Y}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM\otimes^L_{R_X}LN$$
is natural, unital, and compatible with the canonical integer-shift structures. For every $E\in D(R_X)$, the functors $F(P)=RE\otimes^L_{R_Y}P$ and $G(P)=R(E\otimes^L_{R_X}LP)$ are exact, and the natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ adjoint to $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\mu_{RE,P}$ commutes with these shift structures: if $s_F:F(P[1])\cong F(P)[1]$ and $s_G:G(P[1])\cong G(P)[1]$, then
$$s_G\alpha_{P[1]}=\alpha_P[1]s_F.$$
Consequently applying $\alpha$ to a distinguished triangle gives a morphism of distinguished triangles, including its connecting square. These structures are natural in $E$ and $P$; under the tensor-unit identifications $L(R_Y)=R_X$ and $RE\otimes^L R_Y=RE$, one has $\alpha_{R_Y}=1_{RE}$.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] for the bifunctor on derived categories and for checking its natural transformations on K-flat complexes with flat terms. Resolutions with these properties exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to construct the everywhere-defined exact functor $L$, computed by termwise pullback on these resolutions; this includes the required preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, which is not a consequence of resolution existence alone. Smallness gives the Grothendieck module categories and functorial K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Thus $R$ is everywhere defined and triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The underived module adjunction is precisely [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with the module structure on direct image induced by $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$. Apply [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] with $\mathcal A=\Mod(R_X)$, $\mathcal B=\Mod(R_Y)$, $G=f^*$ and $F=f_*$ to get $L\dashv R$, its unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$.

proof.text: For K-flat flat-term representatives $A,B$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies the canonical natural isomorphism $\mu$. Its termwise comparison is the inverse of the extension-of-scalars map $(a\otimes x)\otimes(b\otimes y)\mapsto ab\otimes(x\otimes y)$, whose inverse sends $a\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(a\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$; these balanced maps are the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. In particular $f^*R_Y=R_X$ by multiplication with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $R_Y[0]$ is K-flat: tensor with it is the identity on complexes. Thus $L(R_Y)=R_X$. With the differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the first-factor shift map $A[n]\otimes B\to(A\otimes B)[n]$ is the identity on each summand, and the second-factor shift map $A\otimes B[n]\to(A\otimes B)[n]$ multiplies the summand of first-factor degree $p$ by $(-1)^{np}$. Substitution in $d_A\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_B$ verifies both chain-map identities, including for negative $n$; adding shifts multiplies these signs. Termwise $f^*$ commutes with shifts by the identity, and the displayed balanced maps commute with $(-1)^{np}$. They also commute with chain maps in both variables. Unit compatibility is the equality of multiplication maps on $a\otimes(x\otimes1)$. All these equalities descend by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], giving the natural, unital, integer-shift-compatible $\mu$ on derived objects.

proof.text: Fix a K-flat flat-term representative $A$ of an object. The cone of a quasi-isomorphism $v$ is acyclic; tensoring it with $A$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For a chain map $v:B\to C$, the comparison $A\otimes C(v)\to C(A\otimes v)$ is the identity on $A^p\otimes C^q$ and multiplication by $(-1)^p$ on $A^p\otimes B^{q+1}$. The cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] show that it is a chain isomorphism: in the off-diagonal entry the tensor differential contributes $(-1)^pv$, canceled by the sign on the shifted summand. The inclusion square commutes, and the square for the connecting map $-p$ commutes with the second-factor shift map from step 2. Consequently tensor with $A$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms and sends cone triangles to distinguished triangles after localization; every derived distinguished triangle is isomorphic to such an image by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This proves exactness in the second variable. The graded symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$, checked against the tensor differential, gives exactness in the first variable. Hence $F$ is exact. Exactness of $L$ from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], of tensor just proved, and of $R$ from [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] gives exactness of $G$, with the composite shift structures.

proof.text: Define $H(P)=E\otimes^L LP$, $\beta_P=(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\circ\mu_{RE,P}:LF(P)\to H(P)$ and its adjunction mate $\alpha_P=R(\beta_P)\circ\eta_{F(P)}$, the map adjoint to $\beta_P$; unit, counit and the formula for the adjunct are those of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] applied to the bijection of Step 1. Give $L,R$ the canonical shift comparisons $\varphi^L,\varphi^R$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]; $F$ carries $s_F=\sigma_{RE,-}$, the second-factor shift map of Step 2, $H$ carries $\sigma_{E,L-}\circ(1\otimes\varphi^L)$, and $G=RH$ carries $s_G=\varphi^R_{H(-)}\circ R(s_H)$, all composites as in [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] the pair $(\varphi^L,\varphi^R)$ is compatible with the unit in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique], i.e. $\eta:1\to RL$ commutes with the shift for the composite comparison of $RL$; by part (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] so does $\eta_F:F\to RLF$. By Step 2, $\mu_{RE,-}:L(RE\otimes^L-)\to LRE\otimes^L L(-)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] commutes with the composite shifts, and $\varepsilon_E\otimes1$ commutes with $\sigma$ because the sign maps $(-1)^{np}$ commute with chain maps in the first factor (Step 2), also after whiskering by $L$ (part (iii)); so $\beta$ commutes with shifts by part (i). Then $R\beta:RLF\to RH$ commutes with the composite shifts by part (ii), and $\alpha=R\beta\circ\eta_F$ does by part (i): $s_G\alpha_{P[1]}=\alpha_P[1]s_F$. The same argument with $[n]$ in place of $[1]$ gives the equation for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, compatibly with $[a][b]\cong[a+b]$ since all comparisons used are coherent.

proof.text: Naturality in $P$: for $u:P\to P'$, $\beta$ is natural in $P$ because $\mu_{RE,-}$ is natural [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and $\varepsilon_E\otimes1$ is natural in the second factor; with naturality of $\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], $G(u)\alpha_P=R(H(u)\beta_P)\eta_{F(P)}=R(\beta_{P'}LF(u))\eta_{F(P)}=R(\beta_{P'})\eta_{F(P')}F(u)=\alpha_{P'}F(u)$. Naturality in $E$: for $e:E\to E'$, naturality of $\mu$ in its first variable and of the counit, $\varepsilon_{E'}\circ LR(e)=e\circ\varepsilon_E$, give $\beta^{E'}_P\circ L(R(e)\otimes1)=(e\otimes1)\circ\beta^{E}_P$; applying $R$ and naturality of $\eta$ as before gives $\alpha^{E'}_P\circ(R(e)\otimes1)=R(e\otimes1)\circ\alpha^{E}_P$.

proof.text: Let $P_1\xrightarrow{u}P_2\xrightarrow{v}P_3\xrightarrow{w}P_1[1]$ be distinguished in $D(R_Y)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By Step 3 the image triangles $F(P_1)\to F(P_2)\to F(P_3)\xrightarrow{s_F F(w)}F(P_1)[1]$ and $G(P_1)\to G(P_2)\to G(P_3)\xrightarrow{s_G G(w)}G(P_1)[1]$ are distinguished. The triple $(\alpha_{P_1},\alpha_{P_2},\alpha_{P_3})$ is a morphism of triangles in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]: the first two squares are naturality in $P$ (Step 5) at $u$ and $v$, and the connecting square holds because $\alpha_{P_1}[1]\,s_F\,F(w)=s_G\,\alpha_{P_1[1]}\,F(w)=s_G\,G(w)\,\alpha_{P_3}$ by Step 4 and naturality at $w$.

proof.text: Write $\rho$ for the right tensor-unit isomorphisms $M\otimes^L R_Y\cong M$, $N\otimes^L R_X\cong N$ and $\lambda:L(R_Y)\cong R_X$ (Step 2). Step 2 shows $\rho_{LM}(1\otimes\lambda)\mu_{M,R_Y}=L(\rho_M)$ for the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Hence, by naturality of $\rho$, $\rho_E(1\otimes\lambda)\beta_{R_Y}=\rho_E(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)(1\otimes\lambda)\mu_{RE,R_Y}=\varepsilon_E\,\rho_{LRE}(1\otimes\lambda)\mu_{RE,R_Y}=\varepsilon_E\,L(\rho_{RE})$, i.e. $\beta_{R_Y}=\varepsilon_E$ under the identifications. Then $R(\rho_E(1\otimes\lambda))\,\alpha_{R_Y}=R(\varepsilon_E)\,RL(\rho_{RE})\,\eta_{RE\otimes R_Y}=R(\varepsilon_E)\,\eta_{RE}\,\rho_{RE}=\rho_{RE}$ by naturality of $\eta$ and the triangle identity $R(\varepsilon_E)\eta_{RE}=1_{RE}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. So $\alpha_{R_Y}=1_{RE}$ under the identifications $L(R_Y)=R_X$ and $RE\otimes^L R_Y=RE$.
